llm.answer:
**Core Graphics – Apple Developer Documentation (summary of all key points)** | Topic | Key Take‑aways | Source | |-------|----------------|--------| | **Framework purpose** | Core Graphics is a low‑level, lightweight 2‑D rendering engine built on Quartz. It delivers high‑fidelity output for a wide range of graphics tasks. | [1] | | **Primary capabilities** | • Path‑based drawing (immutable & mutable paths)
• Transformations (affine transforms)
• Color management (color spaces, conversions)
• Off‑screen rendering (layers, bitmap contexts)
• Patterns, gradients, and shading
• Image data handling (bitmap images, masks, creation)
• PDF document creation, display, and parsing | [1] | | **macOS‑specific services** | • **QuartzDisplayServices** – direct control of display hardware via the macOS WindowServer.
• **QuartzEventServices** – manage event taps for observing/altering low‑level user‑input streams.
• **QuartzWindowServices** – query information about windows managed by the WindowServer. | [1] | | **Core data types** | • `CGFloat` – basic floating‑point scalar.
• `CGPoint`, `CGSize`, `CGRect` – geometric primitives.
• `CGVector`, `CGAffineTransform` – vector & transform helpers. | [1] | | **Core objects & classes** | • **CGContext** – the drawing environment.
• **CGImage** – bitmap image or image mask.
• **CGPath / CGMutablePath** – immutable/mutable graphic paths.
• **CGLayer** – off‑screen context for reusable content.
• **CGColor / CGColorSpace** – color components & spaces.
• **CGFont** – glyph & layout information for text.
• **CGPDFDocument** – representation of a PDF file.
• **CGDataConsumer / CGDataProvider** – abstractions for writing/reading raw data buffers.
• **CGShading, CGGradient** – smooth color transitions for radial/axial fills.
• **CGFunction** – callback‑based custom functions.
• **CGPattern** – 2‑D pattern for drawing paths. | [1] | | **Enumerations, constants & functions** | Core Graphics defines a rich set of enums, constants, and C‑style functions for low‑level graphics operations, color space handling, and PDF support. | [1] | | **Platform coverage** | Available on iOS 2.0+, iPadOS 2.0+, macOS 10.8+, tvOS 9.0+, visionOS 1.0+, watchOS 2.0+, and Mac Catalyst 13.1+. | [1] | | **Documentation structure** | The official docs are organized into:
• Core Graphics overview & data types
• Quartz 2‑D programming guide
• Utility & support classes
• Services (display, event, window)
• Enumerations, constants, functions | [1] | **Bottom line:** Core Graphics is the foundational 2‑D drawing engine on Apple platforms, exposing a comprehensive set of primitives, objects, and services for rendering, color management, image handling, and PDF manipulation. It is tightly integrated with Quartz and offers platform‑specific services for display, event handling, and window management.
